cluster_summary: A set of vulnerabilities where user-controlled data is embedded into HTML output without appropriate context-specific output encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML/JavaScript. This occurs when developers assume raw input is safe for direct inclusion in HTML body, attribute, or script contexts.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Apply HTML entity escaping (e.g., StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml, fn:escapeXml, writer.writeText) to all user-controlled values before inserting into HTML body context..

mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs

mechanism.typical_fix: Apply HTML entity escaping (e.g., StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml, fn:escapeXml, writer.writeText) to all user-controlled values before inserting into HTML body context.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Apply HTML entity escaping (e.g., StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml, fn:escapeXml, writer.writeText) to all user-controlled values before inserting into HTML body context.
sub_patterns.name: missing HTML entity encoding in HTML body context
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes user-controlled strings are safe to include directly in HTML text content (e.g., between tags) without HTML entity escaping, allowing injection of arbitrary tags.
